transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-07 14:30 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Narayanan (Orion - Head of Platform), Miguel Santos (Orion - SRE), Dana Li (Orion - Procurement)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on reliability, incident tolerance, and fallback strategies for latency-sensitive payments routing. Orion is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) with particular emphasis on multi-region failover, SLAs, and data residency. Action items captured, agreed to run an early benchmark for multi-region failover.

Topics:
- SLA expectations and uptime targets
- Fallback policies and model variant routing
- Multi-region routing and cross-region failover
- Observability and audit logs for incidents
- Security/compliance docs and procurement next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intros from Redwood side I'm Alex and Samir's our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Priya: Hi Alex, thanks, Priya here, joining from Orion, I run platform, Miguel is our SRE and Dana is procurement.
[00:20] Miguel: hey thanks.
[00:25] Samir (SE): Great, quick call goal is to understand your reliability requirements, what you consider an incident, and how you want failover to behave between hosted/dedicated/private.
[00:36] Priya: Yeah so, high level we do payment auth and routing, so latency is critical, SLAs at least 99.95% for auth paths, but more importantly we need graceful degradation not total failure.
[00:49] Priya: Our current infra is multi-region, primary in us-west2 and failover in us-east1, we also have a small on-prem stack for regulatory data for EU clients.
[00:58] Alex: Understood. What are the tolerances on additional latency in a failover? like acceptable p95 jump?
[01:10] Miguel: ideally p95 shouldn't exceed 300ms above baseline for auth calls, beyond that product flags slow down the pipeline, so it's tight.
[01:21] Samir: Okay we're used to that. We design fallback policies: route to a cheaper/less-capable model or to a regional replica, fallback to cached responses or to a synchronous proxy depending on the route. Quick question: do you need model-level fidelity on failover or can you accept smaller model with same prompt?
[01:40] Priya: We can accept smaller model for non-fraud scoring paths but not for decisioning. For fraud scoring we need deterministic behavior or a tie-breaker process.
[01:52] Alex: Makes sense, so for fraud scoring we recommend Dedicated with pinned model versions and canary rollouts, and also cross-region replicas to keep latency down. For non-critical paths Hosted with automatic fallback to smaller variants could work.
[02:08] Dana: quick procurement question, if we go Dedicated what's the SLA and do you provide credits if SLA is missed?
[02:16] Alex: We have SLA tiers; Dedicated can be contracted to 99.95% with credits in the contract. I'll follow up with the exact matrix.
[02:25] Miguel: Another thing — during incidents we need trace-level logs and request IDs to reconcile payments. Can you push logs to our SIEM or do we pull them?
[02:38] Samir: We support pushing audit logs and traces, plus token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the console. For private/VPC deployments you can also configure retention and forward to your SIEM.
[02:49] Priya: About multi-region: what's the failover mechanism? active-active or active-passive?
[02:55] Samir: Redwood supports smart routing policies: you can choose latency-first, cost-first, or custom policies. For active-active we do request hashing and regional affinity, for active-passive we detect region failure via health checks and route to the passive. We also have automatic fallback to compatible model variants if the exact model isn't available in the target region, that happens by model family mapping.
[03:20] Miguel: health checks frequency and detection windows? we don't want flappy failovers.
[03:26] Samir: Default health checks are 15s, with 3 consecutive failures to consider region degraded, but that's configurable. You can also set stable window and circuit-breaker thresholds for aggressive vs conservative failover.
[03:42] Priya: OK that helps. What about cost implications of keeping replicas in multiple regions?
[03:48] Alex: Yes there's cost: Dedicated multi-region replicas increase reserved capacity needs. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and quantization to reduce per-token cost; you can also configure cold/warm replicas for lower cost. We'll include cost estimates in the pricing doc.
[04:05] Dana: On compliance, we need SOC2 and network diagrams and KMS details.
[04:10] Alex: We'll share SOC2 report and network architecture, plus KMS/HSM integration notes.
[04:16] Miguel: For private/on-prem deployment, how different is the control plane? we need audit logs but also offline capability.
[04:25] Samir: Private gives you a customer-managed control plane, you can run the inference runtime on-prem or in your VPC; audit logs can be sent directly to your collectors. For air-gapped, there's an on-prem package but it adds operational overhead.
[04:40] Priya: We also run internal chaos tests and want to include Redwood in our SRE playbooks. How do runbooks and incident handoffs work?
[04:48] Samir: We can provide a runbook template and a failover test plan. We also support webhooks on incident state changes so your tooling can trigger escalations. We'll collaborate on a multi-region failover rehearsal.
[05:03] Priya: Great. Can you do a short demo of routing policies?
[05:08] Alex: Sure quick screen share, then will capture a recording (note: link to routing-demo deck shared: https://redwood.ai/decks/routing-policies).
[05:15] [demo noises omitted in transcript, reference to deck]
[10:20] Samir: Walking through an example: primary region at us-west2 with a smaller replica us-east1. On failover we prefer regional replica at same model family, if not available we map to quantized variant or cheaper family and mark the call with a fallback tag in logs.
[12:00] Miguel: That fallback tag — will it be visible in our logs so we can reconcile?
[12:06] Samir: Yes, every request has metadata: model_version, fallback_reason, route_region, request_id. We'll push those to your logging endpoint. Transcription note: metadata spelled out as model underscore version sometimes in logs.
[13:12] Priya: On SLA credits, what's the escalation path?
[13:18] Alex: We have a dedicated support tier for enterprise customers; for Dedicated/Private you get 24x7 oncall with an SLO-based escalation, billing credits are calculated per-month for missed SLOs. I'll share the SLA doc and sample contract language.
[13:32] Dana: Procurement will need sample contract and data processing addendum.
[13:36] Alex: yep will send DPA and sample MSA.
[13:40] Priya: One more: during incidents do you have graceful degradation features like prefix caching or KV cache to reduce downstream errors?
[13:50] Samir: Yes we have automatic prefix/KV caching and request-level caching, also dynamic batching controls so during high load we batch more aggressively. For payments-critical endpoints you can pin cache policies to avoid stale data.
[14:06] Miguel: Can we simulate a region outage in a test environment?
[14:11] Samir: Absolutely, we recommend running a chaos test with our test harness; Samir will provide a runbook.
[14:20] Priya: Ok good. Quick risk question: if this is Hosted and Redwood loses a region we route to secondary, is there any PII exposure crossing regions? we have EU data residency concerns.
[14:34] Alex: For data residency we can keep tokens/ePHI in-region; for EU-specific data we recommend Private or Dedicated pinned to EU regions. Hosted can be configured to honor data residency but it's more constrained. We'll include a note in the architecture doc.
[14:50] Miguel: Regarding monitoring, what retention do you provide for traces and logs?
[14:56] Samir: Default retention is 30 days, enterprise add-on for longer retention; for Dedicated/Private you can set retention or export to your storage.
[15:06] Priya: ok next steps?
[15:09] Alex: Recap: we'll send pricing/SLA matrix, SOC2 and network docs, and a demo recording. Samir will draft the failover runbook and test plan. We'll schedule a benchmark the week of 2025-10-20 to test multi-region failover with your SREs.
[15:26] Priya: sounds good, Dana will review procurement timelines and get back on contract questions.
[15:33] Dana: thanks all.
[15:36] Alex: Thanks everyone appreciate the time. We'll follow up with the docs and scheduling links.
[15:42] Miguel: thanks bye.
